chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The worst water on the face of the earth is the water of Barhout, and it is that which is in Hadhramaut, upon which the spirits of the disbelievers drink.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.بَرَهُوتَ: Barhout, a place in Hadhramaut known for its water
key_terms.حَضْرَمَوْتَ: Hadhramaut, a region in southern Yemen

ai.seo_question: What is the worst water on earth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the cosmological significance of Hadhramaut in southern Yemen, linking the physical landscape of the earth to the spiritual state of the disbelievers. In Shia tradition, the 'hamm' (spirits or souls) of the kafir are believed to drink from this specific water source, serving as a tangible sign of their punishment and distinct from the faithful. The narration underscores the interconnectedness of geography and metaphysics in Islamic eschatology.
